title: 5-round AES-128: Five-round function-family distinguisher

target.description: 5 inner AES rounds, without initial whitening and with MixColumns in every round, under fixed round keys. The parameter-independent round argument applies to the standard AES-128 schedule.

setting.key_relation: One unknown fixed key; the underlying inner-round property holds independently of schedule relations.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key restriction.
setting.plaintext_model: One byte takes all 256 values while the other fifteen bytes are fixed.
setting.reference_model: Uniformly random permutation of the 128-bit block space, with the same classical chosen-plaintext access.

time.note: The paper proposes this distinguisher but gives no complete standalone evaluation budget.

preprocessing.note: The 26-byte projected function family is not given a separately costed standalone membership table. The 25-byte attack table in Section5 has different boundaries.

success.description: Advantage of COMPLETE corrected26-byte function-family membership on one ordered256-input active-byte structure. Every fixed-key AES projected vector belongs to a family of at most2^208 ordered byte functions. For a uniform128-bit permutation, each projected byte has2^120 preimages; sequential sampling without replacement and a union bound over the complete family give the displayed finite-permutation inequality. The family uses the actual SB/SR/MC dependency graph and the DTCB09 corrected coefficients, not the erroneous literal DS08 expansions. No random AES parameter, iid projected-byte or independent-test assumption is used. This is derived two-world advantage, not an author-printed numeric rate or equal-prior classification probability. It applies to the complete family, not a sampled/thinned table. Standalone table generation, evaluation time and memory remain unpriced; the separate25-byte key-recovery table and its2^-1848 wrong-sequence estimate are not substituted. The original source-print discrepancy remains attached.

components.description: Propositions2–5: conditional on the intended complete parameterization and correct input coordinate, the actual AES function is included in the complete26-parameter set. This conditional membership does not validate the disputed literal formulas or give an ideal-world false-positive probability.

review.scope: Read DS08 PDF1–11 and DTCB09 PDF1–6; reconstruct the corrected25/26-byte dependency count and exact observable projection. Prove whole-test false alarms by finite-permutation sampling and a union bound at exactly256 distinct preselected queries. All native resources, local components, printed-formula conflicts and audit gates unchanged. Targeted success proof, not a new whole-paper/forward audit.

evidence.locator: FSE2008 PDF3–6/printed118–121 inner-round definition, Propositions2–5 and the26-byte observable projection; targeted success derivation2026-11-07.
evidence.interpretation: Supersedes only the prior absence of a complete ideal-world metric. The corrected full26-byte class contains the AES ordered256-byte vector for every fixed key and has cardinality at most2^208. A fixed output byte vector under an ideal128-bit permutation has probability at most product_{i=0}^{255}2^120/(2^128-i); union over the class gives the stored two-world advantage. This finite-permutation inequality is reviewer-derived, not a source-printed measurement or the later attack wrong-key estimate.

evidence.locator: INDOCRYPT2009 PDF4–5/printed147–148 Proposition3, corrected recurrence and Equations3–6; source states applicability of DS08 is retained.
evidence.interpretation: The existing printed-expansion discrepancy remains recorded. The actual AES dependency graph uses four shared first-round offsets, sixteen second-round offsets, four selected third-round key bytes, one fourth-round output key byte, and one projected fifth-round key byte. Corrected fixed coefficients do not add parameters. The tested family is this complete corrected26-byte class, not the faulty literal equations or later probabilistically reduced classes. No source conflict or native-cost gap is closed by this success proof.

limitations: Results are transcribed from this source version. Full attack searches, costs and success probabilities have not been reproduced.
The general property applies to all key sizes. It does not establish a computational advantage over exhaustive key search for AES-128.

field_conflicts.label: Printed function expansion
field_conflicts.description: The recurrence preceding Proposition2 omits the third-round S-boxes. Printed Equation(1) also differs from the second-round diagonal expressions immediately above it. A separately derived 25-parameter AES factorization passes local component tests; the printed expressions are preserved as discrepant. DTCB09 explicitly corrects Equation1 and the C3_22/C3_44 expansions in Equations2/4, while stating that these errors do not affect DS08 attack applicability. Separate corrected AES factorization is supported, not the literal print.
